<!-- plain-summary -->
An operator can now watch data durability (the custodian's metrics), but the request plane and the capacity plane are still dark: nothing reports how many requests are failing or slow, and nothing reports whether the system is shedding load or running out of room in a failure domain. This adds the minimal per-request and capacity signals proposal 0010 names, so a live deployment shows *service* health, not just *storage* health.

**Parent:** #366 (floor item 4). Spec: proposal 0010 (`docs/design/proposals/draft/0010-observability-floor-for-first-deployment.md`), §"Scope boundary" items 4–5.

## Scope (from 0010)

- **Request-plane RED:** per-op latency + error-by-class on the S3 gateway ops, emitted through the shared `wyrd-telemetry` seam (`DurabilityTelemetry`/`metrics_layer`) that #450 extracted.
- **Capacity-plane signals:** admission admitted / shed / timed-out events, in-flight/stream gauges, per-failure-domain utilization.

## Notes

- The telemetry handle + subscriber wiring at every role entry landed in #527/#531; this item is emission only — the sink already exists.
- Out of scope (0010): dashboards, alerting rules, tracing beyond the floor (span graph → future ADR).

milestone.description: Step 2. Swap embedded redb for distributed TiKV behind the unchanged MetadataStore trait; multi-key atomic directory ops hold under the distributed store. Completes the single-zone data plane — a soft stopping point, not the release: the ★ Step-2 release point is M8 (proposal 0013 implementation arc, supersedes 0002). Plan: proposal 0015 (supersedes 0007; acceptance PR #417); tracker #201; first-deployment gate #367.

title: Emit request-plane RED and capacity-plane signals (observability floor item 4)
